description: Compute the apparent topocentric position of one solar-system body (sun, moon, mercury through neptune, pluto) or a named bright star for an observer location and instant. Returns equatorial (RA/Dec), refraction-corrected horizontal (altitude/azimuth), and ecliptic coordinates, plus distance, apparent magnitude, angular diameter, phase angle, illuminated fraction, angular distance from the Sun, and the constellation it falls in. For a solar-system body it also returns that body card — classification, mean radius, naked-eye visibility — the same values served at astronomy://body/{body}, so a client without resource support does not need a second surface to reach them; a catalog star has no card and the field is absent. Positions are parallax- and aberration-corrected for the given observer; default elevation is 0 m and the default time is now. Supply `star` (e.g. "Sirius", "Polaris") instead of `body` to target a catalog star; `body` is ignored when `star` is set. Pass an IANA `timezone` to also receive the observer-local time. This server does not geocode — resolve a place name to latitude/longitude upstream first.

body.description: Solar-system body to locate. Omit when targeting a named star via `star`.

elevation.description: Observer elevation in meters above sea level. Default 0.

latitude.description: Observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive.

longitude.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive.

star.description: Named star to locate, from a bundled catalog of 32 stars — about 30 of the brightest naked-eye stars plus Polaris, not an arbitrary star. Accepts a common name or Bayer designation, with the Greek letter spelled out or as a symbol and the constellation as its genitive or IAU abbreviation (e.g. "Sirius", "Alpha Centauri", "α CMa"). A name outside the catalog fails with the full list of catalog stars. Takes precedence over `body`.

time.description: Instant of observation as an ISO 8601 UTC string, e.g. "2024-04-08T18:00:00Z". Defaults to now. A value with no zone designator is read as UTC, not the local zone of the server process.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for localized output, e.g. "America/Los_Angeles". When omitted, output is UTC-only.

name: astronomy_get_sky_position

angular_diameter_arcsec.description: Apparent angular diameter of the disc in arcseconds. Null for point-source convention bodies.

body.description: The body or star this position is for, echoed from the request.

body_metadata.description: The body card also served at astronomy://body/{body}, copied here so a client without resource support can reach it. Present for the ten solar-system bodies; absent for a catalog star, which has no card.

mean_radius_km.description: Mean radius in kilometers, from IAU/NASA fact sheets.

naked_eye.description: True when the body is typically visible to the naked eye.

constellation.description: The constellation the body currently falls within.

equatorial.description: Apparent equatorial coordinates, corrected for precession, nutation, parallax, and aberration.

distance_au.description: Distance from the observer to the body in astronomical units.

ra_hours.description: Right ascension in sidereal hours [0,24), equator-of-date.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_time`: The `time` value is not a parseable ISO 8601 instant, or names a calendar date that does not exist (e.g. 2026-02-30). `time_out_of_range`: The requested instant is outside the engine's high-accuracy span (≈1900–2100). `invalid_timezone`: The `timezone` value is not an IANA zone this runtime knows. `star_not_found`: The `star` name is not present in the bundled bright-star catalog. The error lists every catalog star, in the message and as `catalog_stars`. `body_required`: Neither a `body` nor a `star` was supplied. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

horizontal.description: Refraction-corrected horizontal coordinates as seen from the observer.

above_horizon.description: True when the body is above the horizon (altitude > 0).

altitude_degrees.description: Angle above (positive) or below (negative) the horizon, refraction-corrected.

illuminated_fraction.description: Fraction of the disc illuminated, 0 to 1. Null when not applicable.

magnitude.description: Apparent visual magnitude (lower is brighter). Null for bodies where the engine cannot compute it.

phase_angle_degrees.description: Sun-body-observer phase angle in degrees. Null when not applicable (e.g. stars).

sun_elongation_degrees.description: Angular distance from the Sun in degrees [0,180], seen from Earth's center. A body within about 15° of the Sun is lost in its glare. 0 for the Sun itself.

time_local.description: The same instant in the observer-local timezone with offset, present only when a timezone was supplied.

time_utc.description: The instant of the observation in ISO 8601 UTC.

title: astronomy-mcp-server: get sky position
